steps.say: Short bulb narrowings are cut out and rejoined. Defects under two centimetres without dense scarring are repaired by removing the ring and sewing healthy ends together, with success above ninety in a hundred. Removing all scar gives the best lasting opening of any option.
steps.tx: **Bulbar stricture** (bulb urethral narrowing) under **2 cm** (two centimetres) without extensive spongiofibrosis is repaired by **excision and primary anastomosis** (**EPA**, scar removal with end-to-end join), transecting or non-transecting, with success **above 90%** (ninety in a hundred). Removing the scarred ring entirely gives the highest durable patency, so length and tissue quality decide the operation.

vis.alt: Paediatric and reconstructive urology diagram including stricture repair approaches.
vis.caption: Stricture repair approaches including graft onlay for longer defects. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Longer or penile defects need a patch, not removal. Gaps over two centimetres or any penile involvement need substitution with cheek lining, which remains the gold standard patch. Cheek lining is wet, tough, and hairless with rich blood vessels, so it survives in the urethral bed better than skin.
steps.tx: Strictures over **2 cm** or involving the penile urethra need **substitution urethroplasty** (patch reconstruction), with autologous **buccal mucosa graft** (**BMG**, cheek lining patch) as the gold standard material. Cheek lining is wet, tough, hairless, and capillary-rich, so it survives the hostile urethral bed better than any skin graft.

rows: Over 2 cm, or any penile involvement
Any skin graft in the urethral bed

steps.say: The back wall holds patches best. The Barbagli method sews the cheek patch directly onto the tough sheath of the erectile bodies, a flat and bloody surface that gives excellent take. Stitching the patch down stops blood collecting beneath it, and the stiff backing keeps the new channel open.
steps.tx: The **Barbagli technique** (dorsal graft method) applies a **dorsal onlay** (back-wall patch) by fixing buccal graft directly to the **tunica albuginea** (tough sheath) of the corpora cavernosa, a flat immobile vascular bed giving excellent take. Quilting prevents hematoma lifting the graft, and the rigid backing holds the new lumen open through healing.

steps.say: Front wall patches serve the deep bulb. Where thick healthy spongy tissue fills the deep bulb, a front wall patch takes cover without tension from that tissue itself. This path avoids lifting the urethra off its back wall nerve and vessel bundles, trading a softer bed for gentler surgery.
steps.tx: A **ventral onlay** (front-wall patch) fits the proximal bulbar urethra, where thick overlying **spongiosum** (spongy erectile tissue) covers it without tension. This route avoids mobilizing the urethra off dorsal neurovascular bundles at the price of a slightly softer bed for a gentler dissection.

steps.say: Skin patches fail in one skin disease. Lichen sclerosus scars the whole urethra and the opening, and skin flaps from the genitals are strictly forbidden because the disease attacks moved skin too. Cheek lining or staged repairs are used instead, since cheek tissue resists the disease.
steps.tx: **Lichen sclerosus** (long-standing inflammatory skin disease, **BZO** or balanitis xerotica obliterans) scars the whole urethra and meatus; genital skin flaps are banned, a strict **genital skin contraindication** (no genital skin as patch material), because the disease attacks moved skin too. Cheek lining or staged repairs are chosen instead, since buccal tissue withstands the disease.

rows: Genital skin flaps, disease recurs in them

steps.say: The penile urethra must never be shortened. Removing even a short ring from the penile segment bends the organ and shortens it on erection. Patch repair with cheek lining is mandatory here whatever the length looks like, since even a centimetre of loss bends the penis.
steps.tx: **Penile urethral stricture** (penile segment narrowing) must never undergo excision and primary anastomosis (**avoid EPA**, no end-to-end join in penis) because of **chordee risk** (bending deformity) and penile shortening on erection. Substitution urethroplasty with BMG is mandatory whatever the length, since even a centimetre of penile loss bends the organ.

rows: Excision and primary anastomosis in penis
A centimetre of loss bends the organ

steps.say: Destroyed beds are rebuilt in two sittings. The surgeon lays a free patch onto the opened plate first and makes it into a tube months later. This staged path fits repeat failures, failed childhood repairs, and severe skin disease, letting the patch grow blood supply before it carries urine.
steps.tx: **Two-stage urethroplasty** (staged rebuild) by the **Johanson** or **Bracka** technique places a free graft on the opened urethral plate first, then makes it into a tube months later. It is indicated for complex re-operative strictures, failed hypospadias repairs, and severe lichen sclerosus, letting the graft mature its blood supply before carrying urine under pressure.

rows: Free graft laid onto opened urethral plate
Redo strictures, failed hypospadias, severe lichen sclerosus
Blood supply matures before urine load

steps.say: Cutting from inside rarely cures. Slitting the ring with a telescope cures under ten to twenty in a hundred cases once repeated, because the cut simply scars shut again. Rules strongly discourage repeating it after one failure, and repeat narrowings should go to formal patch repair instead.
steps.tx: **DVIU** (direct vision internal urethrotomy, telescopic slit) cures under **10% to 20%** (ten to twenty in a hundred) long-term once repeated, because the slit scars back down. Guidelines strongly discourage a second cut after one **internal urethrotomy failure**; recurrent strictures then belong to formal urethroplasty.
